speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Christopher de Souza, could you take your two cuts together, please?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Mr Chairman, Sir, I beg to move, "That the total sum to be allocated for Head R of the Estimates be reduced by $100." The Ministry of Law (MinLaw) has strategically positioned Singapore to be a legal hub, building on the foundation of the rule of law.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: At this time, ASEAN presents good opportunities to provide an array of legal services.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: China's One Belt One Road Initiative, Thailand's East Economic Corridor and other infrastructure projects also pose great opportunity in the region.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This is especially important for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) which have valuable niche expertise to contribute but may lack the resources to do so.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This disparity, when it comes to technology MNCs, is even more pronounced, with Singapore accounting for 59% and only 18% for Hong Kong.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: One aspect of being a legal hub is being a dispute resolution hub through offering of the whole suite of dispute resolution mechanisms.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The reputation the Singapore International Arbitration Centre (SIAC) has as an efficient and impartial dispute resolution platform has strengthened Singapore's reputation as a dispute resolution hub, servicing the region and even beyond the region.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I should now declare, Mr Chairman, that I am a partner in a firm that practises arbitration.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: SIAC has also been monitoring and spearheading developments in the area of arbitration.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Also involved are the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) and Enterprise Singapore (ESG).

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Would MinLaw please elaborate on the purpose, rationale and thinking behind the Office and how Singapore could benefit from this initiative?

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: Following from the recommendations of the Committee on the Future Economy (CFE) as well as the Industry Transformation Map (ITM) for the professional services sector, what are MinLaw's plans to drive the implementation of the plans and how are we steering ourselves to position Singapore's legal services sector for the future?

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: I have three suggestions on areas for MinLaw to strengthen.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: First, strengthen Singapore as a hub for growth practice areas through targeted strategic marketing and communications.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: Second, strengthen support to both law firms and legal practitioners in their journey to embrace digital disruption, harness technology and regionalise.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: In particular, extra support should be given to small practices, including sole proprietorships, and their staff in their bid to transform.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: Third, strengthen the inhouse counsel community as they are a growing group wanting to further build and enhance their professionalism, competencies and standards, continuing education and career progression.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: They will, therefore, require further support from MinLaw in their drive towards this end.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: I am aware that Singapore Corporate Counsel Association representing the inhouse counsel in Singapore has embarked on and launched their competencies and standards.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: It has been almost a year since the Working Group made its recommendations.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: In particular, I noted many meaningful initiatives have been launched, including TechStart by the Law Society of Singapore and the Future of Law Innovation Programme (FLIP).

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: How many small and medium-sized law practices have been engaged through these initiatives?

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: What has been the impact on the small and medium-sized law practices so far?

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: There was news in the United States (US) about how artificial intelligence (AI) has beaten some top lawyers in reviewing contracts more accurately.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Their contract reviewing algorithm was created by a legal AI platform LawGeex with teams based in New York and Tel Aviv.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Researchers found that the AI was 10% more accurate than humans in spotting key legal issues with business contracts – an everyday task for most lawyers.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Christopher de Souza, please take your four cuts together.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: There is much economic and social advantage to garner from it, including individuals' convenience, accessibility, enterprise, efficiency through innovation, resource utilisation and allocation.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: Society benefits, too, through creating opportunities and finding new ways to generate value.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: To this end, how is MinLaw supporting this effort through the enacting of a supportive legal regulatory framework, or through the day-to-day operations of the various agencies or bodies under its purview?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: Innovation, if harnessed and promoted, can be a key driver of future economic growth.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: This is especially so as Singapore transitions into an innovation-led economy.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: As MinLaw seeks to develop Singapore as an intellectual property (IP) hub, how does it support businesses to develop strategies and expertise to realise the full value of IP?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: Importantly, how do MinLaw and the Intellectual Property Office of Singapore (IPOS) continue to ensure that IP is well protected in Singapore, and that Singapore retains its reputation as a jurisdiction with good IP protection?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: I should also declare that I am a legal practitioner who also practice IP law.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: The rule of law has been called the "bedrock on which our society was founded and on which it has thrived." An accessible court of law is one of the eight non-exhaustive principles which jurist Joseph Raz set out as flowing from the basic concept of the rule of law.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: He says, "Given the central position of the courts in ensuring the rule of law… it is obvious that their accessibility is of paramount importance.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: Long delays, excessive costs may effectively turn the most enlightened law to a dead letter and frustrate one's ability effectively to guide oneself by the law." Access to justice is important for the justice in a rule of law society.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: Justice cannot be exclusive to the well-educated who can understand and navigate their way through our legal system or the rich who are able to hire lawyers.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: Therefore, what reforms does MinLaw envision to improve our criminal, civil and family justice systems, so as to ensure the rule of law and access to justice remain in Singapore?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: There is a need, Sir, to enforce tough laws to deter highly harmful crimes, such as drug trafficking.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: Historically, capital offences were the last category of cases in Singapore to be tried by jury and, later, by two trial judges.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: They were required to arrive at a unanimous decision, otherwise the accused would be convicted for a lesser offence.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: As triers of fact, trial judges have an important role in deciding questions of fact, which the appellate Court seldom disturbs.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
text: In particular, I know that many professional freelancers who are on a contract for service use the SCT when they are not paid for their work.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
text: Raising of the claim limits will be a boon for claimants and freelance workers alike.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Offenders who manage to leave the countries where the offences were committed should not escape justice.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: At the same time, countries that do not have extradition arrangements with others risk becoming magnets for fugitives, which will affect their own security and reputation.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Understandably, one cannot rush into concluding extradition agreements.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: According to the Government, besides the need for a mutual desire for extradition arrangements, the compatibility of the two legal systems is another consideration.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: While I can understand that ASEAN member states overall have very different legal systems, does this mean that there is no plan or desire for an ASEAN-wide mutual recognition of arrest warrants?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: One only needs to look at the case involving David Roach to illustrate the ASEAN challenge.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: With the move towards greater ASEAN integration, the fact that such suspects can go to a fellow ASEAN country to escape justice does not seem acceptable.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: On a more general level, does the Government plan to increase the number of countries which Singapore has extradition agreements with?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Does the Government find it an acceptable coverage?

speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
text: Mr Chairman, international law has been described as a shield for Singapore as a small island-state as well as the occasional sword as well.

speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
text: In addition to interstate disputes, could we know the Government's position on investor-state dispute settlement, and if the Ministry and the Attorney-General's Chambers (AGC) have taken steps to safeguard our sovereign regulatory space against investors' claims?

speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
text: How does international trade law, on the other hand, help the Government to respond to announcements of fresh tariffs by the US Government that have been recently announced, but in consultation with the US, and also on negotiations of the next-generation mega regional agreements, such as the Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP) and the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership (RCEP)?

speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
text: Do developments with private international law as well present new opportunities for Singapore lawyers or that arise from clients in India or other ASEAN countries, as an example?

speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
text: Specifically, what may be the role of lawyers and how are lawyers encouraged to play a role in emerging areas of the regional technology space as well as Smart Nation, as we could see from the cuts that were filed yesterday?

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai (Marine Parade)
text: Mr Chairman, land is not only a finite but extremely scarce resource in Singapore, as this House has been hearing last week.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai (Marine Parade)
text: There are many competing uses of land in Singapore, for industrial, residential, sports, recreation, community, social spaces, each one fulfilling a different but necessary objective.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai (Marine Parade)
text: Judicious and thoughtful land use planning is thus required to strike the right balance and optimise our land resources.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai (Marine Parade)
text: With this in mind, could I ask the Minister for an update on the following?

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai (Marine Parade)
text: First, what considerations are taken into account when allocating land resources and how are the competing interests properly balanced?

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai (Marine Parade)
text: Second, can there be more dual-use facilities, for example, at sports facilities in schools, which can be used on weekends as a dual purpose?

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai (Marine Parade)
text: Third, when is the concept plan next expected to be reconsidered and reviewed, particularly in light of the population objectives and other infrastructural needs that we have?

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai (Marine Parade)
text: They are very quaint, very nice, short low-rise five-storey buildings.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai (Marine Parade)
text: They were built in the 1960s and they are standing till today although the residents have been moved out for the Selective En Bloc Redevelopment Scheme (SERS).

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai (Marine Parade)
text: It would help a lot if we could have it turned into community spaces.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: The process starts with an application to the Court by persons who are willing to administer the estate.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: This is commonly done by lawyers as it is not easy for a lay person to draft such applications.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: The Court would then consider the application and appoint these persons as administrators.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Thereafter, the administrators would have to distribute the estate in accordance with the order set out in the Intestate Succession Act.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: The distribution would generally be to surviving spouses, the deceased's children, the deceased's parents and other family members.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: The main focus of the Court in such cases is to appoint suitable persons as administrators and identify the beneficiaries of the estate of the deceased.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: This is a big relief as, otherwise, the family members of the deceased would be saddled with costs.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I believe there is a case for further simplifying the procedure, especially for straightforward cases involving deceased persons dying intestate and leaving behind spouses and/or children.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Through access to data and data analytics, the Government should be in a position to verify and ascertain the identity of the survivors and their relationship with the deceased without the need for the survivors to go to Court and prove this fact.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: There is, therefore, an opportunity to considerably shorten the administration process without invoking the Court route, which involves time and money.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: This is done in Japan through the family registration system known as Koseki, which I referred to in last year’s COS debates.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: In Japan, estate administration does not involve the courts and is done expeditiously.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: The issue is not just a simple dispute between two neighbours or about an unreasonable neighbour.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: The problem seems to centre on the mental state of a difficult neighbour who behaves irrationally.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: In one of the complaints which I received, the neighbour asked for help regarding a neighbour who rants and uses vulgar language or abusive language on every other resident on the same floor.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: In another case, it was about a neighbour who used a broom stick and banged incessantly on the door of yet another person.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: In a third case, it was a neighbour who hoards rubbish, not just filling up her entire flat, but also in the common corridor.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: The recent case about a neighbour at Block 55 Toa Payoh Lorong 5, reported in the news, who threw corrosive liquid or faeces on the walls is a classic case of one person on that floor terrorising the other neighbours around her.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: There are other media reports which describe other extreme cases of HDB neighbours who make HDB living a nightmare, for example, in Hougang, the neighbour who flung faeces or dung.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: In Yishun, a women kept throwing things like toilet paper, sanitary pads, urine outside the door of another neighbour.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: The question is: what can the authorities do to help the innocent citizens who are adversely affected by the conduct of a mentally unstable person?

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: How effective is this Tribunal in dealing with people who have mental issues and who are not rational?

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: In my opinion, residents who have mental issues require professional treatment, and not just a Tribunal Order.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: They may not have mental capacity as to whether they are behaving unreasonably.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Would these people not simply ignore any order made by the Tribunal?

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: I am sympathetic to families who have to deal with relatives with mental disorder.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: I accept that it is challenging to have such a relative with mental issues.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: However, I am even more sympathetic to the other residents who have to live daily with a neighbour who has a mental issue and is abusive.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: What is the recourse available to these residents?

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Or do they have to live with the antics of a mentally deranged person?

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: This will ensure that any person in need of medical help would be able to find such help for their mental issue and be given regular medication to manage their symptoms.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: This will also provide some form of relief to the other citizens who have to live with a neighbour who is irrational.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Of all the cases dealt with by the Tribunal, does the Ministry track the outcome after the Order is made?

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: How does the Tribunal ensure that quarrelling parties really keep the peace?

speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
text: It is not easy to meet both requirements, and we have all met Singaporeans who applied for, but were found ineligible for legal aid.

speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
text: However, even needy Singaporeans with good claims, who qualify for legal aid from LAB, may not be able to press their claims with LAB's assistance in the following circumstances.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Chairman, in a fair and just society, justice must be accessible to all, including Singaporeans who have less.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Some are less well-informed or less able to put their case across, or even to realise there is a case that could be put across.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Some are less aware of how to seek help.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Some are unaware of the difference between civil and criminal proceedings.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: I have met Clementi residents at my Meet-the-People Sessions (MPS) and on home visits.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Some were worried about the means test for legal aid.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Some were also worried about finding their way around the system, finding out how to seek help.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Separately, can the Ministry help enhance education of the public so that people are more aware of the different ways to find help in different circumstances?

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Has there been any study by MinLaw on how existing processes can be simplified further so that the complexity of finding help does not become an additional barrier for people who want to navigate their way to assistance?

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: We have to ensure that justice is always equally accessible, including to fellow Singaporeans with less.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: While it is heartening to note that a large majority is granted legal aid, there may, nevertheless, be cases that fall through the gaps.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It was stated that the review would include considering granting discretion to the Director of Legal Aid for exceptional cases that do not pass the means and merits test.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can MinLaw provide an update on this review?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Further, how will MinLaw ensure that persons of limited means continue to have access to civil and criminal legal aid?

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Mr Chairman, I thank the Members who spoke.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: I will start with an overview of the legal reforms in our civil, family and criminal justice systems, which Mr Christopher de Souza spoke about.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: In the area of civil justice, my Ministry has been working closely with the Judiciary, legal practitioners.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Mr Patrick Tay asked if we will be raising claims limits in SCT.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: It will allow claims of a higher value, and we hope it will allow claims to be resolved quickly and cost-effectively at SCT.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: On family justice, Members know that in 2014, we made changes.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The reforms brought about several positive developments, including providing a child- and family-friendly approach, where the Courts look at what is in the interest of the children: how best to deal with it, and how to try and move on with as little acrimony as possible.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: We have asked them to review and further enhance the family justice system.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: On criminal justice, I have said earlier during the MHA COS debate that we want a progressive, balanced and modern criminal justice system.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: If Members look at it over the years, there have been a series of reforms, each building on the other: (a) the pre-trial disclosure regime in 2010; (b) the community-based sentences (CBS) which were also introduced in 2010; (c) the changes to the Evidence Act in 2012; and (d) in 2015 – a fairly significant move for the Government – the Government funding legal representation of accused persons through the Criminal Legal Aid Scheme.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: And now, comprehensive amendments to the Criminal Procedure Code (CPC) and the Evidence Act have been introduced in Parliament earlier this week.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Mr Christopher de Souza asked whether we should have three High Court Judges to sit in trials for capital cases.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: We have not seen a need to review this, but it does not mean no.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Members will know that since 2012, if a person is sentenced to death and chooses not to appeal, a confirmation hearing must still be held by the Court of Appeal.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: That ensures that the imposition of the capital punishment is always reviewed by the apex Court of at least three judges.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: So, there is already a two-level process with at least three Judges of Appeal looking at the matter.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: But we will review the point made by Mr Christopher de Souza.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: I will now speak on our commitments towards advancing the international rule of law.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: We see ourselves as a responsible and effective member of the international community, and a firm believer in an international rules-based legal order.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Adherence to the international rule of law is integral to our security and survival.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: To that end, we have done a number of things, which I think the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFA) has spoken about, and which I have spoken about previously.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: So, we do not need to repeat that.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: But we have to continue our engagement with the international community, other states, and our development of international law expertise in relevant emerging issues.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: We should support think-tanks which are doing research in these areas.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Examples are the Asian Business Law Institute and the Centre for International Law, which are supported by us.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: We have to actively participate in international law-making at regional and multilateral forums and bring our interests and values to the table.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: People know our crucial role in the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS).

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: We have led multilateral negotiations on online dispute resolution and dispute settlement.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Right now, we are playing a very important and key role in the United Nations Commission on International Trade Law (UNCITRAL) Working Group II on Dispute Settlement.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The Singapore delegation is well-regarded in the international discussions on insolvency, electronic commerce and recognition and enforcement of judgments.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: We are committed to peaceful international dispute resolution mechanisms.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: These are important for a small country like Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: We serve as a neutral venue for state-related disputes, which is also enabled through the partnerships we have forged, for example, through the Permanent Court of Arbitration and the International Centre for Settlement of Investment Disputes (ICSID), amongst others.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: We also actively participate in discussions on possible reform of investor-state dispute settlement mechanisms, so that any future disputes on trade agreements can be fairly and effectively resolved.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan asked if international trade law will help the Government respond to announcements of fresh tariffs in consultation with the US, and also in our negotiations of the next-generation regional Free Trade Agreements (FTAs), large FTAs.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Well, primarily, how we handle these issues will have to be guided by: (a) what is in our primary, economic as well as strategic interests; and (b) what is the framework of international law, including any applicable treaties.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: That will guide us in taking what we consider to be principled approaches when dealing and negotiating with our trading partners.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: And, of course, in these things, size matters as well.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The second query that Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan had was, "Do developments in private international law present new opportunities for our lawyers vis-à-vis clients in India and the ASEAN countries?" The short answer is yes, they do.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: That is why we participate actively in international efforts to harmonise private international law and to promote the adoption of Singapore legal principles.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Standards, but also any sort of civilised set of standards, in this area, would be welcomed, and it will help us.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: So, that will give our lawyers more opportunities because our commercial law principles are consistent and consonant with international law standards in most advanced jurisdictions.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: I will now deal with Mr Christopher de Souza's question on ensuring Singapore law firms and Singapore-based lawyers remain relevant in the region.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Developing Singapore as a dispute resolution hub is, in fact, one of our key strategies in growing our legal industry.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: I have said that that is a role for the Government but there is also a very critical role for our lawyers.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The Government can provide the infrastructure, the framework, the training through the law schools.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: But ultimately, the lawyers must also take part in it.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: And now the Government is even putting money on the table for law firms to go regional.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Senior Minister of State Indranee Rajah will touch on some of the other strategies, but I will touch on our dispute resolution services.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: We aim to provide a full suite of such services that will create more work for Singapore law practices and Singapore-based lawyers within Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: We have seen, in fact, a tremendous growth in caseload numbers across all our main dispute resolution institutions, such as: (a) SIAC, (b) SIMC, and (c) SICC.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: To promote international commercial mediation, SIMC has also partnered other institutions.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: This is to help businesses resolve disputes that may arise in cross-border transactions under China's Belt and Road Initiative.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: SIMC also signed an MOU with the Japan Association of Arbitrators to help Japan build expertise in international commercial mediation.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: So, how do we ensure that we remain a destination of choice for dispute resolution?

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The starting point is that people must believe and know that there is going to be top-quality legal expertise available here if they come.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: What the Government can do is to make sure our dispute resolution legislation framework is modern and friendly.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: We will continue to make necessary legislative enhancements to make sure that it is at the cutting edge.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: For example, we recently amended the Supreme Court of Judicature Act.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: It clarifies that SICC can hear matters relating to international commercial arbitration under the International Arbitration Act.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: So, it gives the parties who choose Singapore as the seat of arbitration the certainty that they can benefit from the expertise of both local and international judges, who have a wide breadth of knowledge and experience, expertise, and judicial knowledge.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: All of that can be available from the Singapore Courts.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The work itself can only be handled by Singapore-qualified lawyers from Singapore law practices.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: So, they get an international panel of judges.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: We also enacted the Mediation Act in 2017 which strengthens the framework for the enforcement of mediated settlements conducted in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: It codifies certain matters which were previously dealt with under Common Law, such as confidentiality of communications in the context of mediation.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: It provides for greater certainty and clarity for commercial parties who opt to conduct their mediation in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: We will continue to strengthen our international dispute resolution facilities and infrastructure.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: So, obviously it will allow more cases to be heard.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: My Ministry will continue to support the development and expansion of our international law capabilities.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Mr Edwin Tong asked about our plans to optimise our limited land resources.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Mr Christopher de Souza asked about our support of the Smart Nation drive.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The Singapore Land Authority (SLA) has been allowing old state properties with no immediate plans for redevelopment to be innovatively reused.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: So, that gives the buildings a new lease of life.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: It unlocks the value for businesses and individuals.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: It was a former army camp but is now home to a wide range of businesses.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: SLA will continue to find opportunities to convert state properties for different uses, in particular, social and community uses.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: SLA has also opened up previously un-utilised spaces for recreational community use.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Under the Viaduct, they have opened it up.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: SLA provides the platform for geospatial startups and industry partners.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: So, we provide the platform, we make it freely available, people jump on into it and create the business value out of it.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: So, our approach is to enable and support private sector innovation, as part of our Smart Nation efforts.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Mr Chairman, I have covered many different aspects of MinLaw's work.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The common framework for this is, of course, advancing the rule of law and making better use of what resources we have, ultimately, to improve the well-being of the people.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The Senior Minister of State will now take the remaining cuts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Chairman, I thank the Members who spoke.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Singapore was the first in Southeast Asia to enact a legal aid scheme in 1958.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Over the past 60 years, LAB had assisted many low-income Singaporeans in civil legal proceedings.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Many improvements have been made over the years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: First, we have enhanced LAB’s systems and processes to better serve applicants.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: LAB has gone completely paperless with a new case management system, increasing efficiency by allowing different officers to work on a single file simultaneously.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The new system also saves applicants' time, by allowing them to correspond with LAB and submit relevant documents online.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Those who are less IT-savvy, such as the elderly, can continue to correspond with LAB by post or in person.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Staff at the MinLaw Services Centre also assist the applicants to complete, submit and print online documents and forms if they require help.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Second, LAB has established a referral protocol to refer applicants who require non-legal assistance to social agencies and Promoting Alternatives to Violence (PAVE), a family violence specialist agency.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Likewise, these agencies will refer their clients to LAB for legal assistance where necessary.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Such cross-referrals provide better support to the vulnerable and also increases awareness of the aid channels.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In one case, a young lady who had been sexually abused by her father sought help from PAVE.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: PAVE helped her to find shelter and then referred her to LAB to seek a personal protection order (PPO) against her father.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: While LAB handled the legal matters, PAVE provided counselling and emotional support.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The young lady succeeded in obtaining the PPO with the help of PAVE and LAB.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Even as we seek to help more, our guiding principle is that our system should assist those with meritorious cases but who really cannot afford a lawyer.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Chen Show Mao asked if legal aid can be provided for arbitration.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: However, we do not provide legal aid for arbitration, as it is a private, consensual dispute resolution process.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Typically, arbitration is used for high value commercial dispute resolution, and involves much higher costs, compared to Court litigation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We must, therefore, be careful about extending legal aid to such cases.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Nevertheless, there are various existing avenues for individuals to seek assistance and redress.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: (a) LAB can provide legal advice to an applicant on an arbitration clause in his contract and, if there are merits to do so, represent the applicant to challenge the arbitration clause or the arbitration award in the Courts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: (b) Additionally, parties who wish to resolve their dispute by arbitration in a quick and cost-effective manner can consider the Law Society’s arbitration schemes, including its Pro Bono Arbitration Scheme, which adopts streamlined procedures and waives the fees of the sole arbitrator.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In 2017 and this year, we have been working on reforms to the civil justice system.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: When completed, we will be able to review the estate administration system in the context of the civil justice reforms.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Lim Biow Chuan asked about neighbourly disputes involving parties with mental disorders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As a starting point, neighbourly disputes are best resolved amicably between parties, or via community mediation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As a last resort, affected residents may consider filing a claim at the Community Disputes Resolution Tribunals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Tribunals provide a simplified and low-cost avenue for resolving all types of neighbourly disputes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: They are equipped to handle cases involving parties with suspected mental health issues.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Where appropriate, inhouse psychologists and Court counsellors will, first, conduct a preliminary assessment on the individual, and may, with the person’s consent, refer him to the onsite psychiatrist for a preliminary diagnosis and follow-up plan.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In the usual case, a successful applicant will, in the first instance, obtain an Order from the Tribunal.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In the event of non-compliance with the Tribunal’s order, the affected party can apply for a “special direction" directing the respondent to comply with the disobeyed order.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: During the application for a special direction, the Tribunal may order any person, for example, a family member of the respondent, to enter into a bond.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In making this order, the Tribunal may impose conditions or give directions to that person.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: One such direction or condition could be to order a person suspected of mental illness for assessment and/or treatment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: If this special direction is further breached without reasonable excuse, the respondent is guilty of an offence, and the criminal Court convicting the respondent may make a community order against him.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: A community order includes a Mandatory Treatment Order.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Not all mental health cases need be dealt with through the Courts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Persons with concerns about neighbours with mental health issues who may require assistance can contact the Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) and its community partners for assistance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: If the person is a danger to himself or others by reason of his or her mental disorder, the Police can bring the person to the Institute of Mental Health (IMH) for mental health treatment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The person will be warded if assessed to require management in an in-patient setting.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: I will now touch on criminal legal aid.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Criminal Legal Aid Scheme (CLAS) is administered by the Law Society, with support from the Government.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: CLAS assigns a lawyer to accused persons who have been charged with a crime and who cannot afford to hire a lawyer.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: CLAS has also worked to improve its processes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Further improvements include the installation of a direct video-link between the CLAS office in State Courts and Prisons.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: My Ministry will continue to support and work with the Law Society to improve CLAS, just as we have done with LAB.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The continued success of CLAS is only possible with the strong support from the legal fraternity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The CLAS Fellowship, which is generously sponsored by five law firms since 2015, has enabled lawyers to join LSPBS to exclusively handle criminal legal aid cases.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Working Group on Legal and Accounting Services under CFE made several recommendations in this area, which we are in the process of implementing.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: I will outline our plans to capture opportunities in: (a) restructuring; (b) corporations; (c) IP; and (d) projects and infrastructure.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We have moved to strengthen Singapore’s position as an international debt restructuring centre for Asia.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We amended the Companies Act to provide more flexibility and options for corporate restructuring.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We hope to encourage greater use of our legal frameworks and professional services, to facilitate more successful local and international restructurings.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Ministry of Finance (MOF) and the Accounting and Corporate Regulatory Authority (ACRA), together with my Ministry, have been working on enhancing the legal regime for corporations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In 2017, MOF introduced a new re-domiciliation framework to allow foreign companies to transfer their registration to Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This enables them to pursue substantive economic activities here as Singapore companies, while retaining their corporate history.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: ACRA has also set up the Institute of Corporate Law Panel, with industry stakeholders, to provide feedback on corporate law reforms.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: With such feedback, ACRA publishes interpretations of specific legislative provisions, which reduce commercial ambiguity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We have built a robust infrastructure and a good reputation in IP protection, as Mr Christopher de Souza noted.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Our patent office is one of only 20-odd offices in the world that can examine international patent applications under the Patent Cooperation Treaty.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We have also established partnerships with more than 30 foreign IP offices to accelerate patent applications filed in their jurisdictions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Last year, we amended the Registered Designs Act and Patents Act, to keep pace with technology changes, and improve IP protection.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: IPOS has also taken steps to help businesses realise the full value of their IP.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: IPOS, with its partners, have designed programmes to train professionals for high value roles in IP management, strategy and valuation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: These include the Masters of IP and Innovation Management at the Singapore University of Social Sciences (SUSS), and the Professional Conversion Programme (PCP) for IP Professionals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: IPOS' IP Academy has also trained more than 4,000 individuals in areas, such as IP management and commercialisation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In January, IPOS launched the SkillsFuture Study Award for candidates of IP courses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: IPOS also helps businesses develop their IP commercialisation know-how.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: IPOS’s IP ValueLab provides consultancy services on IP audit, due diligence and strategy, to help businesses secure investments for growth.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: To date, IP ValueLab has engaged more than 300 local businesses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Finance Minister announced the setting up of an Infrastructure Office during the Budget Statement.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Projections estimate that US$26 trillion may be spent over the next 15 years on infrastructure projects in Asia.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Many of such projects are looking for financing, and financers are looking for projects to fund.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: But the projects are unable to obtain financing due to lack of bankability, usually occasioned by the lack of proper project preparation, project structuring and technical issues.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Singapore is uniquely placed to address these problems.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We are a leading financial centre, and Singapore-based banks have provided loans or financial advisory services for an estimated 60% of infrastructure projects in ASEAN.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Commercial banks with project finance teams and project structuring expertise are located in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Multilateral development banks, such as the World Bank and its sister agencies, the International Finance Corporation (IFC) and the Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency (MIGA), have also a significant presence in Singapore and offer a critical source of infrastructure finance and project structuring expertise.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We also have accountancy firms with project advisory teams, engineering consultancies, local and international law firms with project financing and infrastructure dispute resolution expertise, and other professional services companies in architecture, engineering and project management.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: My Ministry, through the Professional Services Programme Office (PSPO), will be working with the Infrastructure Office and other agencies, such as ESG, MAS and Economic Development Board (EDB), in this endeavour.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: To access these new opportunities, Singapore lawyers and law firms must also embrace the disruptive changes, reinvent themselves and move up the value chain.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: During a CFE engagement session, I was asked by a Singapore practitioner whether we could protect the wills practice for lawyers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: I suggested in reply that rather than focusing purely on wills preparation, which is an area that can be easily templated and commoditised, he could instead expand his practice and offer a comprehensive suite of services related to wealth management to clients, such as estate planning, and trust and asset management − the legal aspects of it.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Going into high value-added services would gain him access to a bigger market and higher fees.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Of course, he could still continue to do wills as well, as that is part of wealth management.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: My Ministry has been implementing the various strategies from the Professional Services ITM, including (a) technology adoption; (b) internationalisation; and (c) capability development.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: On technology adoption, raised by Mr Patrick Tay and Ms Rahayu Mahzam, we launched "Tech Start for Law" last year to help small and medium-sized Singapore law practices adopt basic technology to increase productivity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The programme covers technology products for practice management, online legal research and online marketing.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This will help Singapore law practices internationalise through overseas mission trips to fast-growing regional countries and workshops.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Law Society will also initiate a marketing campaign later this year to raise the profile of Singapore lawyers abroad.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The programme will be especially useful for the small and medium-sized law practices.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Last but not least, we are supporting Singaporean lawyers in deepening skills and qualifications, through the SkillsFuture Study Awards.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: PSPO will continue to work with Singapore law practices on training and secondment opportunities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In relation to the inhouse counsel community, which Mr Patrick Tay spoke about, my Ministry continues to work with EDB to promote Singapore as a location for companies’ regional and global headquarters, including inhouse counsel teams.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We encourage the inhouse counsel community to continue raising their standards of practice and are heartened by the Singapore Corporate Counsel Association’s recent ground-up efforts in this regard.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Ultimately, the continued success and relevance of Singapore lawyers and Singapore law practices will also depend on how widely Singapore laws and standards are used in commerce and dispute resolution.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: My Ministry is working on the promotion of the international use of Singapore law, standards and frameworks in line with the Working Group recommendations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We strive to incorporate Singapore legal principles and standards at the negotiating table of international platforms, such as ASEAN, the Hague Conference of Private International Law and the UN Commission on International Trade Law.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We also work with international organisations to promote greater understanding and use of the Singapore legal system.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We will also continue to develop uniquely Singaporean legal solutions to serve the international market.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: One example is our restructuring regime mentioned earlier.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: These initiatives will strengthen Singapore’s global market position, build Singapore’s thought leadership, and prepare our legal sector for the future.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: However, the private sector, too, must do its part and get their firms and people ready to compete in this fast-changing landscape.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Chairman, may I beg your indulgence to have a few minutes to complete my response, otherwise, I would not be able to respond to Ms Sylvia Lim’s cut on extradition.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We are, therefore, open to concluding extradition treaties and arrangements.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: All ASEAN member states, including Singapore, are also members of the International Criminal Police Organization (INTERPOL), which provides a platform for international law enforcement cooperation.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We have achieved significant progress and, like many other ASEAN partners, are hopeful that work on this instrument will be concluded as soon as possible.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We have also signed an extradition treaty with Indonesia, which is pending ratification by Indonesia.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: With regard to expanding our network, it is not just a matter of numbers alone.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Negotiating an extradition treaty is not without complexities.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: As Ms Lim has noted, relevant considerations include whether such an arrangement would be mutually beneficial for Singapore and the other country, and whether any divergence in legal systems and procedures can be rationalised.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The volume of requests can place a significant burden on our Government agencies and judicial system.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: More importantly, an extradition arrangement, without adequate protection, carries risks to people in Singapore, including our citizens.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: In summary, we are open to more extradition treaties and arrangements but would take a careful and considered approach.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
text: Can the Minister advise on what the new limits will be, because we know the current limits are $10,000 and $20,000 with mutual consent?

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
text: Has the Ministry decided on how much the new limits will be?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Can I just check with the Senior Minister of State whether discretion can be granted to the Director of Legal Aid when granting legal aid?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: That is one of the things that we will consider in our review.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Would the Member wish to withdraw the amendment?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: I would also like to thank Minister K Shanmugam and Senior Minister of State Indranee Rajah for their insightful replies.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: With that, Sir, I beg leave to withdraw my amendment for Head R.
